title: CYBRIK inference-plane transport-binding common definitions v1
description: Provider-neutral shared primitives for the W2-I inference-plane transport-binding packet: the contract that BINDS the ACCEPTED W2-D provider-neutral inference REST plane to the ACCEPTED W2-F internal service-delegation + mTLS workload-identity seam (ADR-0006 E2/E3; ADR-0008). ADDITIVE to, and DISJOINT from, the accepted v0.1 cross-product packet, the W2-D inference packet, and the W2-F service-delegation packet: this document REUSES accepted primitives from cybrik.common-defs.v1, cybrik.svc-common-defs.v1, cybrik.model-common-defs.v1, and cybrik.data-marking.v1 by $ref and never redefines or modifies them. It carries NO server, host, route, URL, credential, key, or secret. It grants NO model/vendor/tool/agent authority. The core SOC -> Cyber AI seam is versioned REST/JSON over mutually-authenticated mTLS; MCP is a Tool/Agent gateway adapter, NOT a trust boundary here, and does not alter REST inference compatibility. $id uses the RFC 2606 reserved .example documentation domain; it is a stable identifier, NOT an operational endpoint. Status: PROPOSED — NOT ACCEPTED (v0.1.0; not stable v1/GA). Gate W2-I is NOT OPENED and no Founder acceptance has been recorded.

transportProtocol.description: The wire protocol of the core SOC -> Cyber AI inference seam. Const 'rest/json': versioned REST/JSON is the compatibility authority (packet invariant TT-1). MCP is a Tool/Agent gateway adapter, NEVER the inference trust boundary, and is structurally inexpressible here.

httpMethod.description: The HTTP method the inference operation binds to. Only the safe read verb (GET) and the create verb (POST) are used by this plane; no PUT/PATCH/DELETE authority is granted over inference resources.

pathTemplate.description: Internal, versioned path template for an inference operation (e.g. '/api/v1/inferences'). MUST be an internal versioned '/api/v1/...' path; no host, scheme, query, or fragment is carried — this is a mapping token, not an operational URL.

retryDisposition.description: Retry policy for an operation binding. Fail-safe: an operation is retriable ONLY if it is safe (GET) OR idempotency-key-guarded (POST create with a mandatory Idempotency-Key). A non-safe, non-idempotent operation MUST NOT be retried (retriable=false), because a blind retry could duplicate a side-effecting, billed inference. The if/then below makes retriable=true structurally impossible unless one of those two conditions holds.

retriable.description: Whether the client MAY safely retry on a retriable transport error (429/503). Only true when is_safe OR idempotency_guarded.

idempotency_guarded.description: True when the operation is guarded by a mandatory Idempotency-Key so a retry cannot duplicate a side effect.

max_attempts.description: Optional bounded attempt ceiling for a retriable operation.

restBinding.description: Binds one provider-neutral inference operation to its versioned REST verb + internal path, its neutral operation token, and its retry/idempotency disposition. Carries no host or URL. requires_idempotency_key is true for create (POST) operations and false for safe reads (GET).

requires_idempotency_key.description: True when the operation is a create (POST) that MUST carry a mandatory Idempotency-Key (minLength 16). A GET read is false.

allOf.title: TT-4 method/idempotency-policy agreement
allOf.description: The verb and the idempotency policy MUST agree: a create (POST) requires_idempotency_key true, a safe read (GET) requires_idempotency_key false. Without this, a create could declare itself exempt from the mandatory Idempotency-Key and escape replay control, or a safe read could be forced to mint one. httpMethod is the closed GET|POST enum, so the else branch is exactly GET.

decisionId.description: Stable identifier of the relying party's authorization DECISION for a single presented request. Every permit/deny decision on this seam is audited under a decision_id (ADR-0008 D3; packet invariant TT-9); the id is echoed on the response (header + typed error body) so an audit trail correlates the wire decision to its record. Not a credential and not authority.

transportErrorClass.description: Typed, provider-neutral transport/authorization error class for the inference seam. Fail-closed: an unmapped condition MUST surface as 'internal' (HTTP 503-mapped) with no partial authorization, never be silently swallowed. Each class maps to exactly one HTTP status (see httpErrorStatus and the mapping notes). These are TRANSPORT/AUTHZ errors — distinct from the W2-D content-level cybrik.model-inference-error classes (which describe a runtime that produced no result).

httpErrorStatus.description: The typed HTTP status an authorization/transport error surfaces. Deliberately closed set: 400 malformed, 401 unauthenticated/invalid/expired token, 403 authorization denial (audience/pop/tenant/operation/marking/org/issuer/feature), 409 idempotency conflict, 422 semantically invalid request, 429 rate limited, 503 upstream/deadline/internal. No 5xx other than 503 is exposed (fail-closed uniformity).

featureFlagState.description: Feature-flag gating state for an inference operation on this seam. DEFAULT OFF: 'enabled' defaults to false, so a new operation is dark until a Founder/operator turns it on. When disabled, the relying party applies 'disabled_behavior' — it never silently enables. The compatibility behavior for the alert-summarization operation is documented in the mapping notes.

name.description: Vendor-neutral flag token, dotted form, e.g. 'ai.summarization.transport'.

enabled.description: DEFAULT OFF. Whether the operation is currently served on this seam. Absent/false => the operation is dark and disabled_behavior applies.

disabled_behavior.description: Fail-closed disposition when the flag is off. 'reject_unavailable' => the relying party returns a typed 503 feature_disabled error and serves nothing; 'compatibility_passthrough' => the operation is routed to the pre-existing accepted W2-D behavior WITHOUT the new transport hardening being claimed (documented compatibility path only, never a silent security downgrade).

authorizationDisposition.description: The relying party's terminal authorization disposition for a presented request. 'permit' => all bindings held and the W2-D operation MAY proceed; 'deny' => at least one fail-closed check failed and a typed transportError is returned. There is no 'permit-with-warning'.
